cause: -l 7: there is no CPU 7; EAL only accepts CPUs it detected (0-3 here).
fix: Use CPUs that exist: see lscpu or 'EAL: Detected CPU lcores'. Map more lcores onto fewer CPUs with --lcores='(0-7)@(0-3)'.

cause: --memory is not an EAL option. The argument parser prints the problem and exits the process (exit code 234) without returning to main().
fix: Check the spelling against 'app --help' or linux_eal_parameters.rst. Put application options after '--'.

key_line: EAL: Cannot create lock on '/var/run/dpdk/ch04-err-dup/config'. Is another primary process running?
cause: Another primary process already holds the lock on /var/run/dpdk/<prefix>/config. Note rte_errno is not set, so rte_strerror says 'Success'.
fix: Give every independent DPDK process its own --file-prefix, or use --in-memory when no secondary needs to attach. If no process is running, the lock is stale only if the file is held: check with fuser.

trigger: timeout -k 5 15 unshare -m sh -c mount --make-rprivate / && mount --bind $SCR/fakesys/g /sys/kernel/mm/hugepages/hugepages-2048kB && mount --bind $SCR/fakesys/n /sys/devices/system/node/node0/hugepages/hugepages-2048kB && timeout -s INT -k 5 10 ./hello_memory -l 0 --no-pci --file-prefix=ch04-err-nofree
key_line: EAL: No free 2048 kB hugepages reported on node 0
cause: The kernel reports free_hugepages=0 (all pages used by other programs or leaked files). With no usable page size EAL stops; the 'Permission denied' is misleading.
fix: Check grep Huge /proc/meminfo. Remove leaked files (/dev/hugepages/<prefix>map_*) of dead processes, reserve more pages (dpdk-hugepages.py -r 1G), or run with --no-huge for testing.

key_line: EAL: Not enough memory available! Requested: 99999MB, available: 2048MB
cause: -m asks for 99999 MB up front, but the hugepage pool has only 2048 MB.
fix: Ask for less (-m is a pinned minimum, the heap can still grow later) or reserve more hugepages.

cause: The pool has enough free pages, but the --huge-dir mount has a size=64M quota, so mmap() of page 33 fails. With --log-level=lib.eal:debug EAL says: 'attempted to allocate 64 segments, but only 32 were allocated'.
fix: Rerun with --log-level=lib.eal:debug to see which page failed. Check the mount options (mount | grep hugetlbfs), cgroup hugetlb limits, and the -m value.

key_line: EAL: Not enough memory available on socket 1! Requested: 32MB, available: 0MB
cause: --numa-mem 0,32 asks for 32 MB on socket 1; this VM has one NUMA node, so socket 1 has no hugepages.
fix: Ask only for nodes that exist (lscpu, /sys/devices/system/node). On a 2-socket server reserve hugepages on every node you use.

key_line: EAL: Cannot use IOVA as 'PA' since physical addresses are not available
cause: --no-huge memory is ordinary 4 KB anonymous memory: EAL cannot read its physical addresses, so PA mode is impossible.
fix: Drop --iova-mode=pa (EAL picks VA), or use hugepages as root. Non-root without an IOMMU cannot use PA mode at all.

key_line: rte_malloc_socket(..., socket 1) = NULL  rte_errno=0 (not set by rte_malloc)
errno_text: none: rte_malloc returns NULL and leaves rte_errno alone
cause: An explicit socket id never falls back to another node; node 1 has no heap on this single-node VM. (With --no-huge the socket is ignored and the call succeeds.)
fix: Use SOCKET_ID_ANY, or the device's node (rte_eth_dev_socket_id) and check for NULL. Reserve hugepages on that node.
